newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria says EMU criteria open to interpretation.
newsitem.headline: Austria says EMU criteria open to interpretation.

text.p: The convergence criteria for European economic and monetary union are open to political interpretation, Austrian central bank chief executive Adolf Wala said on Thursday.
"Within the treaty, there is political room for interpreting the three percent and the 60 percent criteria," Wala told reporters. "They are not strictly three and not strictly 60 percent."
"It is important to look back into the past and into the future," Wala said.

The Maastricht convergence criteria stipulate that in order to join Europe's single currency, a country's deficit must be no more than 3.0 percent of gross domestic product and debts must not exceed 60 percent of GDP. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12256
